## Interpretation

**One-line verdict:** the geometry-routes-the-change claim replicates cross-recipe and comes out STRONGER, but the exposure account for the end-of-answer clamp BREAKS (registered falsification F2 fires): under the broad 15-negative recipe the clamp is universal — never-negative personas get +13.7 logits of EOS push, more than the trained negatives — and persistence weakens to exactly what the variance ratio predicts.

### H1 — geometry routes the change: REPLICATES, stronger than the parent

- min_dist vs dz (marker-logit change): two-way-FE Spearman **-0.519** (n=557), primary (run-cluster, 16 clusters) CI [-0.687, -0.286]; cell-boot [-0.625, -0.425]; persona-cluster (35) [-0.603, -0.429]; permutation p = 1e-4, Holm p = 6e-4. Parent point: -0.240.
- min_dist vs dmargin (EOS-margin change): **-0.312**, primary CI [-0.575, -0.072]; persona-cluster [-0.387, -0.235]; Holm p = 6e-4. Parent point: -0.271 (inside our persona-axis CI).
- Every clustering axis excludes zero for both channels, so falsification F1 is decisively rejected. More than that: for dz, BOTH the run-axis and persona-axis CIs exclude the parent's -0.240 on the stronger side — the routing is not merely present, it is measurably stronger under the broad recipe. (Cross-panel rho-magnitude comparisons carry a structural caveat: the 16 sources here are heterogeneous by design — 5 persona prompts, 5 query wraps, 1 few-shot scaffold, 5 register rephrases — versus the parent's 80 same-recipe mixes, and the min_dist distribution differs accordingly.)
- Scoping checks all pass (plan §14.6): raw vs FE agree in sign (raw rho -0.391 vs FE -0.519 for dz); never-negative-only stratum -0.524 [run-CI -0.705, -0.272] matches the primary; the A-class-only stratum (172 cells — the direct persona-to-persona parent analogue) is the strongest read, **-0.703** [run-CI -0.889, -0.405, only 5 clusters; persona-CI -0.769, -0.610]. 15 of 16 adapters individually show negative per-adapter rho (-0.86 to -0.29); the one exception is A3 (+0.02).
- Slot-kind sensitivity (plan §14.5): the correlation does NOT live in the emission flip alone. End-of-response-only cells (543 kept, >= 5 EOR slots each): dz rho = **-0.481**, dmargin = -0.217, both perm p = 1e-4. Emission is ALSO geometry-routed: pre_marker slot fraction by distance tercile = 10.1% / 1.4% / 0.8% (closest to farthest), rho(pre_marker frac, min_dist) = -0.25. So geometry routes both graded sub-threshold pressure and outright emission.
- Marker DV in all three spaces (marker-measurement rule): logit dz is the registered channel; log-prob agrees, rho(dlogp, dz) = **0.926** on the primary mask with mean |dlogZ| ~ 1.14-1.19 off the resident cells (saturation localized to the 3 source-resident cells, mean |dlogZ| 2.31) — the logit story IS the log-prob story here. Probability-space sanity: mean ΔP(marker) = +0.886 source-resident, +0.039 never-negative, +0.011 trained-negative — the implant moves ~0.9 probability mass at home and a small but real ~0.04 on never-negative persona cells (in-R emission rate 4.3% never-negative vs 1.3% trained-negative vs 100% source-resident).

### H3 / F2 — the exposure account BREAKS (registered falsification fires)

- Stratum means of dz_eos (EOS-logit change, trained - base): never-negative **+13.66** [run-cluster CI 12.94, 14.32; persona-cluster 12.75, 14.49], trained-negative **+12.46** [run CI 11.76, 13.19], source-resident +2.22 (3 cells, all pre_marker slots).
- H3 predicted trained-negative > never-negative. Observed contrast = **-1.20** [verdict-bearing run-cluster CI -1.62, -0.69; the 3-persona-cluster CI is descriptive only and spans zero]. The gradient the parent's exposure account predicts is absent — in fact slightly inverted.
- **F2 fires by the registered rule:** never-negative mean +13.66 >= the +6.4 cross-panel anchor with the persona-cluster CI [12.75, 14.49] excluding all values below it. The #478 4-negative-recipe analogue on these same 35 personas was **-3.07**. Under the broad recipe the end-of-answer clamp is *universal*: training pushes the EOS logit up ~13-14 logits at the end of the model's own answer for every held-out persona, trained negative or not. Mechanical corroborant: trained-side argmax at the slot is EOS for 95.0% of all slots vs 10.0% for the base at the same slots.
- Scope discipline (plan §14.1): exposure and persona identity are perfectly confounded for the 3 trained-negative personas, so the contrast is descriptive, 3-persona-limited; I do not claim "exposure causes the clamp" — the carried claim is that the prompt-identical negatives show NO predicted excess. Cross-panel anchors (+12.8/+6.4 from #532 context cells; -3.07 from #478 under a 1024 cap) are qualitative reference lines; the load-bearing read is the within-run near-equality of the two strata, which is unambiguous.
- Interpretation: negative-panel breadth changes the clamp's character. With 4 fixed negatives (#478 recipe) the clamp stayed near zero on held-out personas; with 15 diverse negatives the EOS-push generalizes to everyone. The exposure account ("the clamp's level is a training-exposure effect") was a 4-negative-recipe fact, not a general law — ironically the same fate the parent dealt to the context panel's channel claims.

### H2 — persistence: registered bar MISSED; indistinguishable from variance-ratio-only structure

- rho(persona-FE trained z_eos, persona-mean base z_eos) = **+0.891** [persona-boot CI 0.738, 0.970], n=35. The registered success bar (rho >= 0.9 with CI low >= 0.8) is missed on both counts. Parent: 0.969 [0.910, 0.989].
- The calibrated null (plan §14.4; permuted-delta refit) predicts rho = **0.811** [0.705, 0.896] from the observed variance ratio alone (var(FE dz_eos)/var(FE base z_eos) = 0.362). Observed 0.891 sits INSIDE the calibrated null's 95% band. Verdict: the persistence read here is *variance-ratio rank persistence* — the base end-of-answer level still ranks the trained level, but only because the training-induced EOS shift is smaller in variance than the base level spread, NOT evidence of a stronger preservation mechanism. Note the structural change vs the parent: the variance ratio is much larger here (0.36; the broad recipe moves dz_eos a lot), which is exactly why persistence weakened from 0.969 to 0.891. The persistence figure shows visible compression toward the center at high base z_eos (slope < 1).
- Clamp routing: raw rho(persona-FE dz_eos, persona-mean margin_base) = +0.942, but the partial vs margin_base given base z_eos level = **+0.050** (p = 0.776) — it dissolves, replicating the parent's dissolution finding exactly. The complementary partial (base z_eos level given margin) = -0.619 [CI -0.807, -0.227, p = 2e-4]: personas with LOWER base EOS levels get BIGGER clamps — compression toward a common post-training level, consistent with the universal-clamp picture, not margin-specific routing.

### What does NOT replicate (beyond F2)

- **min_dist vs dz_eos:** +0.047, all CIs span zero (persona-axis [-0.053, +0.141]), Holm p = 0.263 — the only family member that fails Holm. The parent's +0.226 [+0.097, +0.354] ("farther personas get a bigger EOS boost") does not transfer: our persona-axis CI excludes the parent point. This is the §14.3 recipe-specificity signature for that channel — coherent with the universal clamp washing out the geometric gradient in the EOS channel.

- **min_dist vs margin_trained:** -0.540 (all axes exclude 0) vs parent -0.082 (spanned 0) — the trained level is geometry-ranked here where it wasn't on the parent panel.

### Holm summary (registered 6-member family; verdicts are CI-only, Holm p diagnostics)

5 of 6 survive (dz, dmargin, margin_trained, margin_base, clamp-routing raw — all Holm p = 6e-4); min_dist-vs-dz_eos does not (Holm p = 0.263). CI verdicts agree with Holm everywhere; no tension to narrate.

### Caveats / scope

1. **Single generation seed, 16 single-seed adapters.** Greedy decoding, one engine seed; run FE confounds adapter identity with its training seed. The run-cluster axis has 16 clusters (5 for the A-class stratum) — primary CIs are honest about this but the run axis is thin.
2. **Truncation + length confound on H1 (the binding caveat for the headline).** Overall generation-truncation rate is 4.28% — NOT zero as the run log claimed — and is concentrated in three A-class adapters (A2 16.1%, A4 18.0%, A5 18.4%). Closer personas truncate more (rho(min_dist, per-persona trunc rate) = -0.355) and longer responses carry bigger dz (rho(response length, dz) = +0.431 on the primary mask). A length/content route into the geometry correlation is therefore not fully excluded by the computed sensitivities (EOR-only excludes emission flips, not truncation): truncated slots are mid-sentence reads where end-of-answer constructs are weakest. The free-analysis follow-up below closes this.
3. **3 source-resident cells excluded** from all correlational reads by design (byte-identical persona/source prompts; saturated implants); used only as positive controls. Sensitivity including them: dz -0.527 (vs -0.519) — immaterial.
4. **Probe-set divergence:** geometry recomputed on q_test_extended_50 (forced — contexts need D-rewrites). Tie-back Spearman 0.9989 over 595 persona pairs: the persona-side metric is the parent's. The context-persona distances (the actual regressor) have no committed reference — an instability there cannot be ruled out by the tie-back, but with H1 strongly positive this caveat is moot for the transfer verdict.
5. **#478-cap comparability:** the -3.07 never-negative anchor was measured under a 1024-token cap vs our 2048; all cross-panel anchor comparisons are qualitative. The F2 verdict does not depend on the anchor's precision — +13.66 vs the anchor +6.4 has the entire persona-cluster CI above it, and the within-run strata comparison carries the exposure verdict regardless.
6. **Rank-correlation scope:** all headline reads are two-way-FE-residualized Spearman (pair-corrected, the parent's convention); raw counterparts are in the hero figure and the raw-vs-FE grid (same sign, FE stronger).
7. **Run-log discrepancy (recorded):** the relayed "truncation rate 0.000 everywhere" claim is contradicted by the committed artifacts (see spot check). No other relayed number disagreed with the JSON.
